Priya K.: heads up — noticed commit usage projection showing APAC reserved commitments undersized for Q2 inference demand. can we do a quick region-fit check? :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Alex M.: on it. which metrics are you looking at specifically? current reserved vs on-demand burn?
Priya K.: exactly. also egress delta and latency SLO impact if we shift more traffic to US regions. APAC spot fill is okay but riskier for p99.
Jorge R.: quick summary from billing + telemetry (last 7d):
```
- apac-east1 (asia-east1): 40 GPUs reserved, avg peak usage 62 GPUs, spot fill ~18 GPUs
- us-west1: 120 GPUs reserved, avg peak 95 GPUs, spot fill ~0
- eu-west1: 80 GPUs reserved, avg peak 70 GPUs, spot fill ~5 GPUs
- egress per TB: apac $140, us $20, eu $35
- avg p99 latency: apac 160ms, us 95ms, eu 110ms
```
Marta L.: oof apac egress killed us. is that total egress or inter-region?
Jorge R.: total egress to customers (most inference responses). internal inter-region egress small but nonzero when we failover.
Priya K.: so two levers: 1) bump APAC reserved to 70ish GPUs (1y commit) to avoid spot losses; 2) route some low-latency-tolerant traffic to us regions to amortize egress — but that adds latency for APAC users.
Alex M.: rough cost delta for option 1 vs 2 (monthly):
```
- Option A (reserve APAC + scale): add 30 GPUs reserved @ $2,200/GPU-month -> +$66k/month, reduces spot interruptions and reduces cross-region egress by ~20%.
- Option B (route 25% APAC traffic to US): increase egress $ by $8k/month but avoid $66k reservation; however p99 for those users goes +70ms.
```
Marta L.: also consider 3y commitment vs 1y. 3y gives ~18% lower rate but locks us. Q3 model rollout might change load shape.
Priya K.: true. we need a middle ground: commit enough to cover p90 peak and keep a small on-demand/spot buffer plus burst lane to hosted. how many GPUs to hit p90?
Jorge R.: p90 ~ 55 GPUs in APAC. So reserving 60 would cover p90 with 5 spare. that's +20 reserved (from 40->60) -> +$44k/mo for 1y vs +$36k/mo if 3y (approx).
SRE Bot: deploy-bot: running a simulation of failover latency impact (ETA 8m).
Alex M.: operational questions: can we set zone affinity so cache warmness stays local? If we shift traffic to US, we lose KV cache locality which increases token computation cost.
Marta L.: good catch — model hotness means more tokens per request if cache missed. estimate adds ~6% token cost when crossing regions.
Priya K.: actionable plan proposal:
- Reserve 60 GPUs in APAC (1y) now to cover p90 and reduce spot churn.
- Create routing rule: route non-interactive batch and low-SLA evals to US/EU to reduce egress/mo. Keep interactive/low-latency in APAC.
- Add metrics alert for spot eviction > 5% sustained -> trigger reserved increase playbook.
Jorge R.: I'll run precise cost delta numbers with model token penalty and updated egress numbers, put into spreadsheet.
Alex M.: I'll mock the routing rule and run a small canary (10% traffic) to US tomorrow morning. Will also measure KV miss penalty.
Priya K.: thx, can we reconvene after the canary? aiming for decision by EOD Fri.
Marta L.: +1. Also recommend we ask finance if we can use shorter 9-month commit trial (vendor supports flexible term) before a 3y lock.
SRE Bot: simulation finished: failover p99 increases by +42ms when shifting 25% APAC traffic to US; overall error-rate unchanged.
Priya K.: perfect — that matches expectations. Jorge, Alex, please post numbers here when ready. I'll open a PR for reserve request (cost approval) once we confirm monthly delta.
Alex M.: will do. also flagging potential supply constraints — a couple providers report limited spare A100s in the APAC zone for near-term procurements. Might speed decision.
Jorge R.: adding that to spreadsheet. ETA 2h.
Marta L.: thanks team. if commit approved, ops will prepare quota increase runbooks and a rollback plan (scale down route override to 0%)
Priya K.: closing loop: decision by EOD Fri, canary tomorrow, numbers in 2h. :thumbsup:
